key_insight: A hybrid SNOMED CT search system can safely combine exact lexical matching with semantic retrieval so each method handles the query types it is best at without weakening the other.
clinical_relevance: This could make clinical term entry and concept lookup faster and more robust for both typed partial phrases and paraphrased clinical language, using SNOMED CT’s own descriptions.
method: Multi-prefix lexical search + BioLORD-2023-M semantic retrieval
Reciprocal Rank Fusion to merge rankings, with optional BGE re-ranking
Local LLM-based query normalization/entity extraction and optional hierarchy filtering
evidence_signal: The system was evaluated on 542 Spanish disease mentions from DisTEMIST in zero-shot conditions, with additional testing on 12,897 English discharge-note mentions from a SNOMED CT entity linking challenge.
watch_item: Performance may depend on query normalization, ranking fusion, and the quality of the local vocabulary/LLM components, so errors in one stage can still affect retrieval if not carefully controlled.
paper_title: Hybrid lexical-semantic retrieval over SNOMED CT: combining two retrieval paradigms to facilitate clinical data entry
